sections.title: Description
sections.content: You are a wizard! Shrunken Down is a fast-paced action platformer built in 96 hours for the GMTK Game Jam 2026. You jump, slash, and shoot your way through monster-filled caves racing to find a cure for your shrinking - the smaller you get, the harder it becomes to defend yourself, so every second counts. The game plays with the jam's theme through an inventory that shrinks along with you, forcing constant decisions about which weapons and items are worth keeping.

sections.title: The Jam
sections.content:
I built Shrunken Down with my friends Ayden and Spencer as team Project Zeta. We developed the whole game in Godot over one weekend - designing, programming, and polishing a complete gameplay loop with multiple weapons, spells, and randomly generated levels. I focused heavily on the game's user interface, having to solve interesting problems in making such a heavily UI focused game still feel fast paced an intuitive. I am particularly proud of the automated dual hotbar system, allowing users to control spells and weapons at the same time, and intuitively activate and select them without worrying about opening their inventory to organize it all during gameplay.

When judging our game, players praised the weapon variety and the tension of managing an ever-shrinking backpack, with one reviewer describing it as feeling "like Hollow Knight with an AK47" (as a Silksong fan, a massive compliment). Out of ~10,000 entries, Shrunken Down placed in the top 800 for Enjoyment, putting us in the top 8% of entries.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: Itemize streamlines how you decide what to cook with what you have — even when you have no idea where to start. Our team spent a lot of time staring into our fridges, unsure what to make or even what we actually had, so for our ShellHacks 2024 submission we decided to tackle exactly that. Itemize arose from a desire to bring order to one of the most important — and most expensive — parts of our daily lives.

sections.title: Building the App
sections.content: Itemize uses SwiftUI for all frontend functionality and a PHP backend for planned cloud storage. At its core, the app leverages the GPT API to analyze receipt scans, categorize items, and suggest new recipes. Much of our time went into crafting a flow that felt natural without being too simplistic to be useful — a balance that was difficult to strike, but one we're proud of. Our MVP is fully functional, and the result is an app every member of our team would genuinely use. It was most rewarding to see how our combined efforts came together into such a complete product.

sections.title: The Future
sections.content: Throughout this hackathon, we each had the chance to work with genuinely useful technologies — SwiftUI and PHP among them — as well as explore new areas like Progressive Web Apps. Everything we gained will be invaluable as we continue developing Itemize. Looking ahead, we plan to fully integrate our backend cloud storage and expand the app to a multi-platform experience. The core flow will largely stay the same, but additional modalities, UI refinements, and expanded capabilities are all on the roadmap.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: Gizmo is your digital bridge between your phone and your computer, transforming the way you interact with your devices. With Gizmo, you can seamlessly execute actions on your computer right from your phone — making multitasking effortless. Whether you want to launch a Siri shortcut, trigger a keyboard command, or insert a frequently used text snippet, Gizmo has you covered. Designed with user-friendliness in mind, Gizmo lets you customize and create your own actions tailored to your exact workflow. No more juggling between devices or navigating complex menus — a few taps on your phone and your computer responds instantly.
Customization

sections.title: Modalities
sections.content: One of the key advantages of Gizmo being an app rather than a physical device — like the Stream Deck — is that it can be configured in nearly infinite ways. I wanted to make sure I leaned into that when building it, so customization was always at the forefront of development. Every action can be bound to a unique input type: button, toggle, knob, or dragger. Each was designed to be intuitive and easy to configure, so users can set up their workspace quickly. Inputs can be styled however a user likes, and placed or resized freely anywhere on their screen.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: POOSDKer is a semester-long project I built with my classmates. We developed a fully functional poker game in SwiftUI, complete with custom networking infrastructure to support local multiplayer.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: StoryForge is my group's submission for ShellHacks 2023. It's a web app that lets users play Dungeons & Dragons with an AI dungeon master who tracks the full game state while shaping a dynamic story. Players can interact however they like by typing freely, and we layered in quality-of-life quick actions as well as on-screen environmental effects that react to where they are in the game.

sections.title: How We Built It
sections.content: We built a web app that walks the user through setting up their character and making decisions throughout the adventure. Every player choice is routed to the ChatGPT-4 API, which we configured to return structured JSON responses representing different game states and branching outcomes.

sections.title: Inspiration
sections.content: Our inspiration came from Dungeons and Dragons — a game we all love, but one with no real way to play solo. We wanted to build a version you could experience by yourself, with an AI that brings the full dungeon-master experience to life.

sections.title: Challenges
sections.content: Our biggest challenge was getting the ChatGPT API to return consistently structured JSON we could reliably parse, while ensuring our prompts contained enough context to produce the gameplay experience we were after.

sections.title: What We're Proud Of
sections.content: We're proud of how effectively we used Git to stay coordinated and maintain clean version control throughout the project. Getting the ChatGPT-4 API working cleanly was also a real win — there was a surprising amount of conflicting information out there on how to implement it properly.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: Dequeue is my team's submission for a semester-long hackathon hosted by KnightHacks. The idea was drawn from the Stream Deck — a device streamers use to trigger shortcuts and macros from a dedicated panel. Rather than memorizing every shortcut or buying expensive hardware, Dequeue lets you display and execute shortcuts right from your phone. The app was built with React Native for mobile and Electron for desktop, enabling it to run across multiple platforms with ease. All data is stored locally on the computer and transmitted to the phone over LAN.

sections.title: Inspiration
sections.content: The Stream Deck — an expensive piece of hardware that lets streamers program macros and trigger shortcuts from a dedicated panel — was our starting point. We asked ourselves: could we build something that does the same thing using just a phone and a computer, without the price tag?

sections.title: Challenges
sections.content: Our main challenge was figuring out the best approach for communication between the phone and the desktop. We also spent significant time getting the desktop app to accurately capture key input — particularly ensuring it could detect modifier keys alongside character keys.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: WikiWhat is a game I built for my friends and me. The goal is simple: given only images pulled from a wikiHow article, guess which article they came from. The game randomly fetches an article and its images, then surfaces the names of several incorrect articles as decoys. Building it involved a lot of work in game design, database development, and writing a Python backend.

sections.title: Description
sections.content: Meets Stories is a web application that lets users create and share stories with their friends. Users build stories by uploading images and videos, then share them with their social circle. The project was built using React, Node.js, Express, and MongoDB.
